rationale: Closed the last unobserved half of the main account: whether the stale membership view survives a later configuration change. The two-mode harness now adds a voter after the long run, through a current-configuration leader, and samples the restarted node's configuration, its applied writes and the conflict index again. Local construction feedback: the new configuration entry is processed by the restarted node (its view becomes {A,B,C,D,E,F}), while the entry at the conflict index remains different across nodes and the restarted node's FSM still holds the write only the minority side accepted. So the stale membership lasts until the next configuration change, while the entry and applied divergence needs a snapshot install.

scope.description: The two-mode five-node restart scenario with the healed phase extended by a long run and then by a real configuration change: after roughly two hundred further committed entries a current-configuration leader adds voter F and the restarted node is sampled again.
assumptions: All state comes from normal operations, and the configuration change is issued through valid ConfigurationChangeCommand handling (AddVoter) with a five-second enqueue timeout.
The added voter F has no running instance, which is legal for the operation under test and leaves the commit quorum reachable through the five live nodes.
The configuration change is issued after the long run, so it is a new entry for every node, including the restarted one whose view was stale.
Exact indexes are not asserted; the event reports operands for inspection.
excluded: No membership removal, demotion or further change is made; only one AddVoter.
The repair phase that follows still uses harness-arranged lag.

experiment.prefix: The helper builds the five-node cluster with in-memory transports, stores and MockFSM, bootstraps {A,B,C} from A, elects a leader, transfers leadership to A if needed, applies three commands, snapshots A, starts D and E, adds both as voters, applies a further command and emits 'fixture'. It shuts A down, cuts {A,C} from {B,D,E}, reconnects A to C only, restarts A with the mode's feature setting and emits 'restart'. It waits for a leader per partition, writes once on each leader, reads the shared index and emits 'outcome'. It reconnects the mesh, waits for one leader, applies one entry and then 200 further entries, waits until the leader's log has advanced at least 150 entries past the conflict index and emits 'healed' with payloads, applied writes, configurations and the long-run operands. It then ensures a current-configuration leader, calls AddVoter for F with a five-second timeout, waits 300ms and emits 'reconfigured' with the leader, the error, the restarted node's configuration and applied writes, the payloads at the conflict index and whether they agree. The repair phase follows as before. The test runs mode defect_restart first and control_no_restore second, so the event order is fixture, restart, outcome, healed, reconfigured, repaired, then the same six events for the control.
semantic_changes: After the long-run healed sample the harness ensures a current-configuration node leads (transferring leadership to B if needed), adds voter F with a five-second timeout, waits 300ms and emits 'reconfigured' with the leader, the change error, the restarted node's configuration, its applied writes and whether the entries at the conflict index agree.
Five comparisons are added over the 'reconfigured' event in both modes.
experiment.responsibility: hashicorp/raft configuration handling: a configuration entry is processed on AppendEntries whenever it is a new entry, independently of the log scan that a restart performs, so the stale view ends at the next membership change while the conflicting command remains.

comparisons.description: Feature on: a new configuration entry should refresh the restarted node's view, ending the stale membership.
Feature on: the entry at the conflict index should still agree across nodes after the configuration change.
Feature on: the restarted node should still hold the write only its own side accepted.
Feature off control: the same configuration change should be reflected.
Feature off control: entries should remain consistent.

experiment.revision_reason: Adds a configuration change after the long run and a 'reconfigured' event, so the question of whether a later configuration entry refreshes the restarted node's view is answered in the same execution; the earlier phases and their comparisons are unchanged.
